items.title: Correct current Coax and Psionic capability claims
items.body:
## Problem

The current compiler catalogue records modules, qualified imports, visibility, evidence, generic procedures and fixed-array value parameters, while older explanatory prose still calls several of them unavailable. Psionic also needs current compiler and GPU qualification limits described consistently.

## Scope

First, bounded child of the existing book-accuracy issue. Correct stale capability and navigation claims in the Coax and Psionic books against current main, preserving dated historical evidence. State the current limits of generic structs/constraints, scalar-only foreign calls, borrow checking, native check execution, target layouts and GPU execution. Fix README/SUMMARY discoverability. Keep library API indexes, new recipes and product migrations in coax-library-contract-recipes.

## Acceptance

- A reviewable claim table links every corrected capability to current source/catalogue or retained qualification evidence.
- Both books' structure/link checks pass; executable example gates run only for examples actually changed, otherwise cite retained unchanged evidence.
- Implemented, partial, planned and unavailable behavior are distinguished; no current capability is called absent merely because its general form remains planned.
- Historical measurements retain dates and scope; no test is reported as newly rerun without execution.
- No product code, library public API promise, issue identity/status/claim or broad formatting changes are bundled into this patch.

Complete and push within one two-hour task; commands stay below fifteen minutes. This child does not close the broader library-contract/adoption task.

items.title: Carry typed GPU records and storage views through checked lowering
items.body:
## Problem

Verse shader uniforms and Psionic tensor/kernel arguments repeat shape, offset, stride and access information across Coax declarations and platform launch/binding code. A matching byte count or successful generated shader compilation does not establish typed resource layout or the complete execution contract.

## Scope

Workstream 7 of the cross-book audit. Carry an explicitly bounded subset of typed parameter records and storage-view metadata from the checked graph into actual GPU lowering and target-specific ABI/layout records. Select one real Verse graphics resource and one Psionic compute argument path; retain their arithmetic, workgroup rules, ownership and GPU lifetimes. Reuse the target/profile manifest and existing backend-conformance machinery. Keep direct WGSL pipeline migration in r8-direct-wgsl-layouts; this issue is not completion of that separate emitter contract.

## Acceptance

- Supported record fields, numeric storage views, shape/stride/access rules and target layout profiles are specified before implementation; unsupported records/aliases/stages fail with original-source diagnostics.
- Generated size/alignment/offset/stride/binding facts agree with independent native/device observations for each claimed target.
- The selected real Verse and Psionic consumers use the generated typed facts instead of independently maintained launch/layout copies; outputs and numerical tolerance rules are unchanged.
- Available claimed backends execute bounded upload/kernel/readback fixtures, including a deliberately wrong field/stride/access case; unavailable hardware and unsupported forms remain explicitly unqualified.
- Existing authority/mutation gates and lifetime/fence/error-path checks remain effective; no shared-memory/barrier or full-backend support is inferred from CPU checks.

## Limits and implementation sequencing

This is an umbrella. Before implementation split it into acceptance-complete slices that each finish and push within two hours; keep this issue open until all consumer and device gates above pass. Do not broaden resource/interpreter/crypto budgets or waive missing device execution. Protocol identities and signed original bytes remain unchanged.

items.title: Refuse a native pass when the evaluator baseline failed
items.body:
## Measured gap

The initial native helper from 3ea326018c returns passed/exit 0 for its eligible #test subset while the same source contains a failing #forall baseline. Ordinary coax test --library exits 1; the native subset record omits that quantified check. Frozen proof: /tmp/coax-native-baseline-audit.json. Existing coax.native-checks.v1 deliberately means subset differential agreement, including matching failed assertions/traps; preserve that historical meaning.

## Scope

Add a versioned strict companion/verdict before expanding native check emission. Retain the complete compiler-owned evaluator baseline for original source bytes and explicitly name unsupported or unexecuted native claims. A failed, exhausted or missing baseline must not become a strict native pass. Preserve the existing parent claim and historical 62-check result. This host-tool correction does not complete compiler-owned native policy.

## Acceptance

- Retain the exact passing-test/failing-quantified-baseline source as a check-first regression. The strict invocation returns nonzero, names the failure with physical provenance and preserves the evaluator witness.
- Tests cover failed/inconclusive/missing baseline observations, unsupported native coverage and a fully passing supported file.
- Preserve normal evaluator budgets and mandatory authority checks; no resource increase makes a case pass. Test original bytes with library mode, rather than relabeling a synthetic-main graph as the original baseline.
- Keep legacy v1 differential semantics identifiable. New strict meaning/fields use a new contract version; coax.evidence.v1 remains evaluator evidence.
- Push focused code and evidence within two hours, then continue native emission/execution/domain/semantic/consumer children. Commands stay below fifteen minutes.
